speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, I need to know your age and when these symptoms first started. Do you have any family members who also experienced similar balance or coordination issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing recent onset gait instability and limb clumsiness, particularly on the right side. To better assess the progression and nature of your ataxia, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as worsening symptoms during fatigue or heat, or any associated sensory changes like tingling in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast to evaluate for PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy).
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial and sagittal views.
Given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, I am highly concerned about PML, a serious opportunistic infection. Can you confirm how long you have been on this medication and if you have recently had your JCV antibody status checked?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain findings demonstrate lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.
